title: Hollow
author: Brian Catling
review:
3.5/5 man I was so hyped on this one and it had such a promising start to about the halfway point and just didn't progress or develop in a way that built any sort of tension or depth. There were a couple of world building revelations that were just dropped in with exposition and not revealed in a natural way and that's when I started worrying.

Initially I was concerned about the length because it's established as a big world and had three distinct and interesting POVs and I was guarding myself about wanting more in the end, but I ended up just taking away that it whimpered out instead of leaving me on a high and wanting more.

The foundation was so great though, really think this could've been an all-time favorite if it built up in a better way and had better plotting, connected me to the characters better, and built upon the themes more. The writing is great, the world building is weird, dark, and brutal; taking a lot of inspiration from art, history, literature. The plot also makes sense and it's not so weird that it's hard to keep track of.

Just a really perplexing experience of the best foundation to a story that doesn't develop or go anywhere meaningful, pretty disappointed overall. I might give him another chance with one of his other works, but this didn't give me confidence on him delivering a fully satisfying story.
